"'''Weak'''" is a song by American [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] vocal trio [[SWV]] from their debut studio album, ''[[It's About Time (SWV album)|It's About Time]]'' (1992). It was written and produced by [[Brian Alexander Morgan]], who composed the lyrics based on a young person falling in love for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Frederick|first1=Brendan|title=Interview: Brian Alexander Morgan, the '90s Mastermind Behind SWV, on His History & Return to Music|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2014/09/brian-alexander-morgan-swv-interview|website=complex.com|publisher=Complex Magazine|access-date=March 29, 2015}}</ref> Inspired by his crush on singer [[Chanté Moore]],<ref name="complex">{{cite web|first=Brendan|last=Frederick|title=Interview: Brian Alexander Morgan, the '90s Mastermind Behind SWV, on His History & Return to Music|url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/brendan-frederick/brian-alexander-morgan-swv-interview|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=September 22, 2014|access-date=August 2, 2023}}</ref> Morgan originally wrote the song for [[Charlie Wilson (singer)|Charlie Wilson]], but he later decided to give the song to SWV. Morgan later revealed that lead singer of SWV, [[Coko]], did not like the song and gave him attitude during the recording of the single.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Greene|first1=Andy|title=The WTF Comeback of SWV|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/the-wtf-comeback-of-swv-20140220|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=February 20, 2014 |access-date=March 29, 2015}}</ref> Coko, in turn, said that she did not like the song because she found it difficult to sing initially because the song forced her to do things she was not used to.<ref>{{cite web |title=0:01 / 5:53 SWV "Weak" Official Lyrics & Meaning - Verified |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tRpUMM5D8b0 |website=Genius | date=March 31, 2023 |publisher=Youtube |access-date=18 October 2024 }}</ref>

A partially re-recorded version of "Weak" was released in April 1993 by [[RCA Records]] as the third [[Single (music)|single]] from the album. It topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for two weeks in July 1993, as well as the [[Cash Box Top 100 Pop Singles|''Cash Box'' Top 100]], and sold over one million copies domestically and was awarded a [[Music recording sales certification|platinum]] certification from the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). It also topped the ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B Singles]] chart for two weeks. Outside the US, the single reached number six on the [[Recorded Music NZ|New Zealand Singles Charts]] and number 33 on the [[UK Singles Chart]]. ''Billboard'' ranked the song at number 72 on their list of the "100 Greatest Girl Group Songs of All Time".<ref>{{cite magazine|title=100 Greatest Girl Group Songs of All Time: Critics' Picks|url=https://www.billboard.com/media/lists/100-greatest-girl-group-songs-7857816/|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=July 11, 2017}}</ref>

"Weak" is a song by American R&B vocal trio SWV from their debut studio album, It's About Time (1992). It was written and produced by Brian Alexander Morgan, who composed the lyrics based on a young person falling in love for the first time. Inspired by his crush on singer Chanté Moore, Morgan originally wrote the song for Charlie Wilson, but he later decided to give the song to SWV. Morgan later revealed that lead singer of SWV, Coko, did not like the song and gave him attitude during the recording of the single. Coko, in turn, said that she did not like the song because she found it difficult to sing initially because the song forced her to do things she was not used to.

A partially re-recorded version of "Weak" was released in April 1993 by RCA Records as the third single from the album. It topped the US Billboard Hot 100 for two weeks in July 1993, as well as the Cash Box Top 100, and sold over one million copies domestically and was awarded a platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). It also topped the Billboard Hot R&B Singles chart for two weeks. Outside the US, the single reached number six on the New Zealand Singles Charts and number 33 on the UK Singles Chart. Billboard ranked the song at number 72 on their list of the "100 Greatest Girl Group Songs of All Time".

sections.wikitext: Sheet music for the song "Weak" shows the key of [[D minor]] with a tempo of "slow groove" at 63 beats per minute.<ref>[https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0101375 Weak] Musicnotes.com</ref>
sections.text: Sheet music for the song "Weak" shows the key of D minor with a tempo of "slow groove" at 63 beats per minute.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Pan-European magazine ''[[Music & Media]]'' described "Weak" as a "lush [[ballad]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1993/MM-1993-06-12.pdf|title=New Releases: Albums|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=10|issue=24|date=June 12, 1993|page=11|accessdate=October 29, 2021}}</ref>
sections.text: Pan-European magazine Music & Media described "Weak" as a "lush ballad".

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.wikitext: "Weak" was included in [[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'s "53 Best R&B Songs of the '90s".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/the-best-rnb-songs-of-the-90s/ |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |title=53 Best R&B Songs of the '90s |date=November 3, 2022 |access-date=March 6, 2026}}</ref> In 2026, American girl group [[Girlset]] sampled the song in their single "Tweak".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Is this GIRLSET’s moment? |url=https://www.thefader.com/2026/03/06/girlset-tweak-song-breakthrough-moment |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text: "Weak" was included in Pitchfork's "53 Best R&B Songs of the '90s". In 2026, American girl group Girlset sampled the song in their single "Tweak".
